findings.title: The operating_point gate cannot fail
findings.detail: calibrate_power raises unless |rise - 60| <= calibration_tol_K (0.25 K), so every value that reaches ctx.op is already within 0.25 K. The gated ±1 K operating_point check can therefore never fail. The behaviour is safe (a miss becomes an error result, never a verdict), but this sanity check gives no independent assurance.
findings.evidence: e009_run.py calibrate_power returns only when abs(rise - tgt) <= tol; run_layout appends abs(cal - target) to ctx.op; gated_checks compares that against operating_point_tol_K = 1.0.
findings.suggested_check: Say in the spec that operating_point is implied by calibration, or gate on the recomputed rise_lv0_K over the dies.

findings.title: F4 leakage guard only compares the sealed seed with two dev seeds
findings.detail: full() refuses only if the sealed seed equals dev_seed or smoke_fresh_dev_seed. Nothing checks the three fresh fingerprints against layouts already used in development (E006's fresh layouts, the T0243 dev-study layouts, the seed-7 smoke layouts). A collision is unlikely with an mfos-sealed seed, but the objective says the fresh layouts were 'never used before', and that is asserted rather than checked.
findings.evidence: fingerprint_check tests only dev fingerprints == config, one fresh layout per family, and 5 distinct fingerprints.
findings.suggested_check: Record the known development fingerprints in the spec and assert the fresh ones are not among them.

findings.title: Registered-run path (full()) is not exercised by the smoke run
findings.detail: The smoke run never calls ExperimentRun. An API mismatch would first appear on the burst VM. I checked by reading the code: the run.metric/sanity/domain/rows/notes/seed calls match mfos.evidence.ExperimentRun. All 15 declared sanity names are reported (the smoke meta.checks list matches the spec's sanity_checks), and all 18 spec metrics are recorded in full().
findings.evidence: tools/mfos/mfos/evidence.py signatures; the smoke meta checks list has 15 names equal to the spec's.
findings.suggested_check: Run full() once ad hoc with MFOS_SPEC_JSON/MFOS_SEED set to a dev seed on the smoke overrides before burning VM hours.

findings.title: fem_rule_file_sha256 is recorded in the spec but never checked by the runner
findings.detail: fem_rule_frozen instead checks content equality (config.fem_rule == the file on disk) plus the production constants, which is the stronger check. The recorded hash does match the file (0226b770...0e9a).

independent_checks_performed: Ran the DoD spec/config check by reading the code, and ran 'uv run mfos exp check E009 --rows research/e009/dev_rows.json': exit 0. The F3 null (dT_const_k) gives 0.0251 scaled and 2.52 K, so it fails both A1 and A2 as required.

Re-ran the full smoke pipeline into $TMPDIR, so no repository file was touched: exit 0, peak RSS about 2.6 GB. It reproduces all 106 committed dev rows (fem_lv0-2, l2_lv1-3, T_ref, dT_const_k, power_w) to a max abs difference of 1.3e-10, and the same calibrated powers (31.834748 W, 46.903655 W).

Checked the per-material volume-mean temperatures used to pick the constant-k null's conductivities on a dev layout. _layer_means (which relies on mesh.t element order matching np.nonzero(g.mat >= 0)) agrees with an independent computation from node_value at the structured lattice corners, all 7 materials to 1e-5 K.

Checked the runner's constant-k override (_const_k_solve: kfun replaced, then _solve_grid(constant_k=True)) against production solve_layout(constant_k=True) with the same k: max |dT| = 0.0 (bitwise identical); amg_gs_sweeps = 2 and energy balance 9e-15.

Read thermal_fem._solve_grid, layout_grid, solve_layout, box_stack_grid, _build_mesh and thermal_layout.solve_layout_level/build_layout_grid. Both solvers get the same power, h, coolant, k(T), die order and uniform die-top flux, and Tj max is a top-surface quantity in both. Die indexing between FEM tj_max and L2 die{i} is consistent.

Checked that mfos.metrics.max_gci_consistency with ref_gci_cap = 0.25 matches the runner's per-row a3_ratio logic (F5 makes A3 +inf, divergent gives +inf, zero estimate with nonzero difference gives +inf), and that the A4 recompute (where is_finest) covers both case and crosscheck rows, as the objective requires.
Checked that E006's Stats.lines and _gate_max are real checks: bisection of every axis, and NaN/inf gives +inf so the gate fails.
Hashed frozen_config.json: it matches fem_rule_file_sha256. The reference_sha256 check (canonical payload hashes befc5efa/ca05847b) passed in my smoke re-run.
caveats: Everything checked here is plumbing and physics consistency, on coarsened smoke grids. Whether the frozen Q1 rule meets A1/A2/A4 and node_count_growth on the frozen grids rests on T0243's dev study (level 2 on the burst VM), which I did not reproduce.
The registered-run path full() was checked only by reading the code against the ExperimentRun API. It has not been executed end to end.

The cost and memory figures for the fresh layouts (9.3 h scikit-fem, about 105 GB for FV level 3) are extrapolations (marked [S] in the note). The 45 h timeout and n2-highmem-32 sizing depend on them.

F5 is implemented as ref_gci_cap inside the A3 metric (A3 becomes +inf, so INCONCLUSIVE), not as a gated sanity check. This matches the objective's F5 response and I0099, even though the objective's detection text says 'gated check'.
The runner uses private thermal_fem names (_solve_grid, _materials, _count_nodes). A rename would fail loudly, and the code is covered by the code_under_test hashes.
